efile.text: Weekly payers must file and pay via electronic means. Monthly payers with an average Rhode Island withholding for the previous calendar year of $200 or more per month must file and pay via electronic means.

deposits.interpretation: Rhode Island sets the payment frequency from the tax withheld in a calendar month: $600 or more in any month is a WEEKLY payer (and stays weekly until the start of a calendar year); $50 or more but less than $600 is a MONTHLY payer; less than $50 is a QUARTERLY payer. Moving to a less frequent basis is allowed only at the beginning of a calendar year; a higher amount moves the employer up at once. The frequency is therefore an INPUT or is derived from a supplied monthly liability. Due dates are NOT computed from a rule: the booklet prints a 2026 calendar of every weekly period (Sunday to Saturday, cut at each quarter end), every month and every quarter with its due date, and this profile holds those printed rows. Pay dates in any other year draw an error finding (state_calendar_not_published) and no due date is invented. Monthly payments are due the 20th of the next month (June: July 31 and other quarter-ending months: the last day of the month after, with Form RI-941); weekly payments the next banking day after the week (generally Monday, Tuesday after a holiday); a quarter-end stub week is printed with its own date. Two printed weekly rows deserve a look against the PDF: the period June 21-30 is shown due Friday 2026-07-03 (the observed Independence Day holiday) and July 1-4 due Tuesday 2026-07-07; the stored text cannot show the calendar's colour coding, so they are used as printed.

returns.name: Form RI-941, Employer's Quarterly Tax Return and Reconciliation
contents: Filed by the last day of the month after the quarter by every employer; quarterly payers send it with the payment.
Weekly and monthly payers use it to reconcile the quarter's payments; it is filed even if no tax was withheld in a quarter-ending month.

Electronic filing is required for weekly payers and for monthly payers averaging $200 or more a month; others may file on paper unless the business has $5,000+ of combined annual tax liability or over $100,000 of gross income.
Bulk filing is by Payroll Letter of Intent to Tax.VendorForms@tax.ri.gov, after which the contact receives a PIN notice and the Administrator User Guide.

returns.name: Form WTM (RI-941M), monthly return for non-quarter-ending months
contents: Only for monthly payers who are not required to file electronically; due on or before the 20th of the following month.
Electronic monthly payers make the payment only.

returns.name: Rhode Island W-3 reconciliation of all returns
contents: Due January 31, or at the termination of business: reconciles the weekly, monthly or quarterly returns with the W-2s and with the payments for the year.
W-2s are due to the State by January 31 and must be filed electronically (EFW2, .txt, ASCII) by employers with 25 or more Rhode Island employees or any claiming a Rhode Island tax credit.
1099s with Rhode Island income must be filed even with no Rhode Island tax withheld.

returns.name: Quarterly Tax and Wage Report (Form TX-17)
contents: Due on or before the last day of the month after the quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31); the regulation moves a due date that falls on a Sunday or legal holiday to the next business day, and the postmark determines the date of receipt.
An employer that fails to report or pay when required may be put on monthly reporting at the Director's discretion (260-RICR-40-05-1, 1.7).

notModelled: The regulation names Sunday and legal holidays only: a due date on a Saturday is not addressed, so this profile moves it to the next business day, which may be later than the regulation requires.

The Employer Tax Unit's own pages refuse automated access and were not read: the TX-17 form, its electronic-filing threshold (25 or more employees per a search summary), and the penalty schedule are not modelled.
The profile wage base is $30,800; the TX-17 also lists $32,300 for employers with an experience rate of 9.19 or higher (DOL compilation), which is not modelled.
The agency's file format specifications, penalties not quoted above and portal enrollment steps were not read.
